item.title: Controllable Spoofing Attacks on Visual SLAM in Robotic Vehicles
item.description: This work investigates security vulnerabilities in Visual SLAM systems used by robotic vehicles, presenting controllable spoofing attacks that can precisely manipulate vehicle navigation and localization.

item.title: When Audio and Text Disagree: Revealing Text Bias in Large Audio-Language Models
item.description: This work investigates the behavior of Large Audio-Language Models when audio and text inputs provide conflicting information, revealing a systematic text bias that has important implications for model reliability and safety.

item.title: Oedipus: LLM-enchanced Reasoning CAPTCHA Solver
item.description: Oedipus demonstrates the vulnerability of reasoning-based CAPTCHAs to LLM-powered attacks, highlighting the need for more robust human verification mechanisms in the age of advanced AI.

item.title: PhyScout: Detecting Sensor Spoofing Attacks via Spatio-temporal Consistency
item.description: PhyScout introduces a practical approach to detecting sensor spoofing attacks by analyzing the spatio-temporal consistency of sensor data, providing robust protection for autonomous systems against adversarial manipulation.

item.title: VisionGuard: Secure and Robust Visual Perception of Autonomous Vehicles in Practice
item.description: VisionGuard presents a practical approach to securing visual perception systems in autonomous vehicles, addressing critical vulnerabilities that could be exploited by adversaries in real-world scenarios.

item.title: PentestGPT: Evaluating and Harnessing Large Language Models for Automated Penetration Testing
item.description:
This work introduces PentestGPT, a groundbreaking approach to automated penetration testing that harnesses the power of Large Language Models. The tool addresses the long-standing challenge of automating security testing by leveraging LLMs’ extensive domain knowledge and reasoning capabilities.

Key Features:

  • Three-Module Architecture: Reasoning, Generation, and Parsing modules that work together to emulate human penetration testing workflows
  • Real-World Evaluation: Comprehensive benchmark using actual penetration testing targets and CTF challenges
  • Significant Performance Gains: 228.6% improvement in task completion rates compared to baseline GPT-3.5 model
  • Community Impact: Over 6,500 GitHub stars demonstrating strong industry adoption

Technical Innovation: PentestGPT addresses critical challenges in LLM-based security testing, including context loss and task-specific reasoning. The framework systematically breaks down complex penetration testing scenarios into manageable sub-tasks, enabling more effective automated security assessments.

Open Source Impact: The tool has been successfully deployed in real-world penetration testing scenarios and has fostered an active community of security professionals and researchers, validating its practical value in both academic and industrial contexts.

item.title: Glitch Tokens in Large Language Models: Categorization Taxonomy and Effective Detection
item.description: This work provides a systematic study of glitch tokens in Large Language Models, establishing a categorization taxonomy and developing effective detection methods to improve the reliability and security of LLM systems.

item.title: Source Code Summarization in the Era of Large Language Models
item.description: This work examines how Large Language Models are transforming source code summarization, providing insights into their capabilities and limitations for automated software documentation.

item.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Jailbreaking ChatGPT via Prompt Engineering
item.description: This workshop paper provides practical guidance on jailbreaking ChatGPT through prompt engineering, offering insights for both attack and defense research.

item.title: PonziGuard: Detecting Ponzi Schemes on Ethereum with Contract Runtime Behavior Graph (CRBG)
item.description: PonziGuard introduces Contract Runtime Behavior Graphs for detecting Ponzi scheme smart contracts on Ethereum, providing more accurate detection than existing approaches.

item.title: MASTERKEY: Automated Jailbreaking of Large Language Model Chatbots
item.description:
This work presents MASTERKEY, a systematic approach to understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities in Large Language Model chatbots. The framework introduces novel methodologies for automated jailbreak attack generation and provides comprehensive analysis of existing defense mechanisms.

Key Contributions:

  • Novel time-based attack strategy inspired by SQL injection techniques
  • Automated jailbreak prompt generation achieving 21.58% success rate
  • Comprehensive evaluation across mainstream chatbots (ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat, Ernie)
  • Systematic analysis of defense mechanisms in commercial LLM services

Impact: This research has informed major service providers about critical vulnerabilities and contributed to strengthening LLM security measures across the industry.

item.title: A Comprehensive Study of Jailbreak Attack versus Defense for Large Language Models
item.description: This work provides a comprehensive study of jailbreak attacks and defenses for Large Language Models, establishing benchmarks and providing insights for the development of more robust LLM security mechanisms.

item.title: PANDORA: Jailbreak GPTs by Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning
item.description:
Distinguished Paper Award

PANDORA introduces a novel attack vector against RAG-enhanced LLM systems. By strategically poisoning retrieval databases, attackers can effectively bypass safety mechanisms in models like GPT-4, highlighting critical security considerations for RAG deployments.

item.title: Digger: Detecting Copyright Content Mis-usage in Large Language Model Training
item.description: Digger introduces methods for detecting whether copyrighted content has been used to train Large Language Models, providing tools for addressing legal and ethical concerns in AI development.

item.title: NAUTILUS: Automated RESTful API Vulnerability Detection
item.description: NAUTILUS introduces an automated approach to RESTful API vulnerability detection, addressing a critical gap in web security testing. The framework combines static specification analysis with intelligent dynamic fuzzing to discover security vulnerabilities in modern web APIs.

item.title: SoK: Rethinking Sensor Spoofing Attacks against Robotic Vehicles from a Systematic View
item.description: This Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) paper provides a comprehensive overview of sensor spoofing attacks against robotic vehicles, establishing a taxonomy of attack methods and analyzing the effectiveness of various defense mechanisms.

item.title: Prompt Injection Attack against LLM-integrated Applications
item.description: This work systematically investigates prompt injection vulnerabilities in LLM-integrated applications, revealing critical security risks and providing recommendations for secure LLM deployment.

item.title: Jailbreaking ChatGPT via Prompt Engineering: An Empirical Study
item.description: This work presents the first comprehensive empirical study on jailbreaking ChatGPT through prompt engineering, identifying key vulnerability patterns and providing insights for improving LLM safety mechanisms.

item.title: Automatic Code Summarization via ChatGPT: How Far Are We?
item.description: This work provides an empirical evaluation of ChatGPT for automatic code summarization, assessing its capabilities and comparing against existing approaches.

item.title: The Threat of Offensive AI to Organizations
item.description: This work examines the growing threat of offensive AI to organizations, providing a framework for understanding AI-powered attacks and developing effective defenses against this emerging threat landscape.

item.title: On the (In)Security of Secure ROS2
item.description: This work presents the first comprehensive security analysis of ROS2’s security mechanisms. We discovered multiple vulnerabilities in the Secure ROS2 implementation that can be exploited to compromise robotic systems, highlighting critical security issues in modern robotics middleware.

item.title: Morest: Model-based RESTful API Testing with Execution Feedback
item.description: Morest introduces a novel approach to RESTful API testing that combines model-based testing with execution feedback, enabling more effective test generation and vulnerability discovery.

item.title: An Investigation of Byzantine Threats in Multi-Robot Systems
item.description: This work investigates Byzantine threats in multi-robot systems, presenting attack methodologies and detection mechanisms for securing collaborative robotics applications.

item.title: Novel Denial-of-Service Attacks Against Cloud-based Multi-Robot Systems
item.description: This work investigates security vulnerabilities in cloud-based multi-robot systems, presenting novel denial-of-service attacks that can disrupt robot coordination and mission execution in distributed robotics applications.

item.title: Efficient Password Guessing based on a Password Segmentation Approach
item.description: This work introduces a segmentation-based approach to password guessing, demonstrating improved efficiency in security analysis tasks.

item.title: A Fog Computing Based Approach to DDoS Mitigation in IIoT Systems
item.description: This work introduces a fog computing based framework for DDoS mitigation in Industrial IoT systems, providing distributed defense capabilities at the network edge.
